title: Number of Black Blocks
summary: Given a grid of dimensions m x n with some cells colored black, where the black cells are specified by a 2D integer matrix of coordinates, count the number of 2x2 submatrices (blocks) that contain exactly 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4 black cells.
statement: Given a grid of dimensions m x n with some cells colored black, where the black cells are specified by a 2D integer matrix of coordinates, count the number of 2x2 submatrices (blocks) that contain exactly 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4 black cells. The result is an array of five integers, where each integer corresponds to the count of blocks containing a specific number of black cells.
constraints: An m by n grid contains black cells at the distinct coordinates; all others are white.
For k from zero through four, count 2-by-2 blocks containing exactly k black cells.
Return the five counts in that order.
hints: Each black cell affects at most four neighboring 2-by-2 blocks.
Count black incidences keyed by valid block top-left coordinates.
Bucket nonzero block counts and derive zero blocks from total blocks minus touched blocks.
Every black cell contributes once to each containing block, so the stored incidence is exactly that block’s black-cell count.
editorial: Every black cell contributes once to each containing block, so the stored incidence is exactly that block’s black-cell count.

The only 2-by-2 block contains exactly two black cells.
